svg.desc: 1. Accepting the order and limiting the rate 2. Creating the order and reserving stock 3. A temporary payment failure 4. Backoff and first retry 5. Backoff and second retry 6. Confirming the order and responding 7. Asynchronous fulfillment 8. Giving up and quarantining

g.text: The token bucket decides whether to allow the request
The saga starts and the order becomes PENDING
Stock is reserved for each item
With stock reserved, payment is requested
The provider is asked to authorize the charge
Sent again with the same idempotency key
Sent again with the same idempotency key
Tells the customer the order is complete
The event is delivered to the worker
Calls the warehouse API up to three times
The failed event is set aside for review
Accepting the order and limiting the rate
The gateway checks its rate limit counter, then forwards the order to the Order Service.
Creating the order and reserving stock
The Order Service moves the order to PENDING and reserves stock.
The payment provider returns 503. The Payment Service does not give up, and switches to retrying.
After one second, the request is sent again with the same idempotency key. The outage continues.
The wait doubles to two seconds, and this time the payment succeeds.
The order is confirmed. The customer's response and the event are sent at the same time.
The worker receives the event from the queue, and retries on its own if the warehouse API fails.
An event that fails all three attempts goes to the dead letter queue, so it does not block the queue.
